entry.title: Azure/azure-sdk-for-net - Releases - 2026-11-26
entry.content:
Azure.ResourceManager.NetApp_1.20.0

1.20.0 (2026-11-24)

Features Added

  • Upgraded the default service API version to 2026-09-01. Subvolume operations continue to use 2026-08-01 by default.

Breaking Changes

  • The 2026-09-01 service API no longer exposes the geographic namespace origin, asynchronous directory deletion, or bucket Key Vault user-assigned identity settings from 2026-08-15-preview.
  • The wire value of NetAppLdapServerType.OpenLdap is now OpenLdap rather than OpenLDAP, matching the service specification.

Other Changes

  • Marked the legacy subvolume types, operations, volume properties, and model factory overloads as obsolete. They remain callable for existing applications.
  • Marked the legacy Entra ID configuration models, account properties, and model factory overloads as obsolete. They remain callable with a service API version that supports Entra ID configuration.

Azure.Messaging.WebPubSub.Chat_1.0.0-beta.2

1.0.0-beta.2 (2026-11-25)

Features Added

  • Regenerated the client from service API version 2026-08-01-preview, now the default.
  • Added pageable listing of rooms, users, topics, and rooms associated with a user.
  • Added topic creation, retrieval, merge-patch updates, and conditional soft deletion, with topic lifecycle states and conversation metadata.
  • Added UpdateTopicOptions and typed topic update methods returning the updated topic.
  • Added UpdateMessageOptions for partial message updates, including explicit null assignments to clear the creator or content.

Breaking Changes

  • Renamed WebPubSubChatConversation.ParentRoom to RoomId, including the model factory parameter; the wire property remains parentRoom.
  • Renamed typed create-or-replace request parameters from resource to role, room, member, user, and topic.
  • The typed UpdateMessage and UpdateMessageAsync overloads now accept UpdateMessageOptions instead of WebPubSubChatMessage. The RequestContent overloads are unchanged.
  • Create message content with WebPubSubChatMessageContent.FromText or FromBinary instead of a parameterless constructor and writable properties.
  • Removed the initial continuationToken parameter from next-link pageable list methods. Resume paging with AsPages(page.ContinuationToken) instead.

Azure.ResourceManager.ContainerServiceFleet_1.4.0-beta.1

1.4.0-beta.1 (2026-11-16)

Features Added

  • Upgraded the service API version to 2026-11-02-preview.
  • Added identity binding profile management and an Apply operation to apply identity bindings to fleet members selected by label.
  • Added configurable allowed-failure thresholds for update stages and groups, and failure counts in update run, stage, and group status.

entry.title: dotnet/SqlClient - Releases - 2026-11-26
entry.content:
Stable Release v8.0.0

The driver and its four companion packages are version-aligned at 8.0.0. Use matching versions of all installed family packages. The family AssemblyVersion is 8.0.0.0; .NET Framework applications upgrading from 7.x should review strong-name binding redirects. Native SNI and Microsoft.SqlServer.Server remain independently versioned.

Companion package release notes

  • Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.AlwaysEncrypted.AzureKeyVaultProvider 8.0.0
  • Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.Extensions.Azure 8.0.0
  • Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.Extensions.Abstractions 8.0.0
  • Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.Internal.Logging 8.0.0

Changes Since 8.0.0-preview1

Changed

Breaking default change: pool waits share the connection timeout budget

What Changed:

  • Switch.Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.UseOverallConnectTimeoutForPoolWait now defaults to true. SqlConnection.Open and OpenAsync carry the remaining Connect Timeout budget through pool acquisition and login with either pool implementation. (#4642, #5030, #5046)

Who Benefits:

  • Applications under pool contention no longer grant login a fresh full timeout after waiting.

Impact:

  • Opens may time out sooner. Set the switch to false before using SqlClient to restore the prior separate budgets; the switch is cached on first use. Connect Timeout=0 stays infinite. This does not claim that every remaining in-open round trip has been converted. See networking migration guidance.

Lower destination-metadata cost for name-mapped bulk copies

What Changed:

  • SqlBulkCopy restores fast SET FMTONLY ON; SELECT * discovery for destination-name mappings, with one catalog fallback if a name is missing. Destination-ordinal mappings, implicit/default mappings, and SQL Graph aliases use catalog discovery directly. (#4985, #4988, #5036)

Who Benefits:

  • Repeated name-mapped bulk loads avoid unnecessary catalog-query work on the server.

Impact:

  • Automatic mode preserves hidden-column positions and graph-alias support. Fallback happens before rows are sent; it does not retry the write.
  • Switch.Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.UseBulkCopyCatalogMetadataDiscovery=true always uses catalog discovery and avoids fallback for hidden-name workloads. Explicit false never uses catalogs and uses visible-column positions, without hidden-column or graph-alias discovery. Leaving the switch unset selects automatic mode.

Asynchronous command execution awaits enclave attestation

What Changed:

  • Asynchronous command execution now awaits enclave-session lookup, attestation preparation, session creation, and retry-time invalidation, including the shared reader, nonquery, scalar, XML, APM, and batch paths. Caller cancellation reaches enclave-provider operations. (#3672, #4887, #5066)

Who Benefits:

  • Always Encrypted applications avoid blocking on attestation-service I/O in async execution.

Impact:

  • Preparation failure or cancellation stops the user query from being sent and releases setup state. Synchronous execution retains synchronous provider dispatch.
  • Key-store operations, enclave-package generation, cryptography, and serialization can still run synchronously. This is not end-to-end asynchronous Always Encrypted support. See asynchronous enclave attestation.

Dependency and authentication-diagnostic updates

  • Updated Azure.Core to 1.65.0, MSAL and its broker to 4.92.0, and the applicable .NET 10 dependency floors to 10.0.15. The exact per-framework direct dependencies are listed below. IdentityModel, Key Vault Keys, and legacy polyfill versions are unchanged from preview1. (#5031, #5041)
  • Updated native SNI dependencies from 8.0.0-preview1.26309.4 to 8.0.0. (#5144, #5146)
  • Authentication configuration/registration diagnostics now use resources owned by Abstractions. Existing translated messages move with their satellite assemblies; messages without a translation fall back to English. Exception types and authentication contracts are unchanged, but exact message text can change. See the Abstractions companion notes. (#4852, #5044)

Fixed

  • Fixed managed networking deadlocks when opening connections on a single-worker scheduler. Parallel SQL Browser (SSRP) requests now run on the default scheduler, and Strict TLS authentication completes without capturing the blocked caller's scheduler. (net10.0, managed SNI only) (#5147, #5148)

  • Fixed ExecuteXmlReaderAsync and BeginExecuteXmlReader observing the first attempt while an invalid enclave session is being retried. Completion now follows the retry's outcome, and a successful retry releases the original asynchronous reservation. This avoids competing reads of the TDS response, misleading XML/protocol errors, and failed connection reuse. (#5117, #5136)

  • Removed a socket-poll wait from pooled TCP connection health checks, avoiding an approximately 15 ms delay when reopening healthy idle connections on Windows with managed networking. Peer-close detection is retained. The nonblocking check also runs on Unix, where the old timeout already rounded down to zero. Native SNI and .NET Framework are unaffected. (net10.0, managed SNI only) (#5070, #5071, #5099)

  • Fixed managed TCP sends after connection disposal reporting an unexpected NullReferenceException instead of the existing connection-error path. (net10.0, managed SNI only) (#5067, #5076)

  • Fixed managed SNI TLS handshakes ignoring the remaining login timeout, which could block Open/OpenAsync and pool users for minutes when a server or network stalls after PRELOGIN. This bounds the handshake, not every separate pool-wait behavior. (net10.0, managed SNI only) (#4834, #5045, #5051, #5078)

  • Fixed SqlTransaction.Dispose() throwing NullReferenceException or InvalidOperationException when it races the background close of a connection broken by a network failure or an unacknowledged command timeout, obscuring the original error. (#4971, #4972, #5053)

  • Fixed late SqlBatch cancellation errors being hidden by ArgumentOutOfRangeException when the last command has already completed. Valid command attribution is preserved. (#5042, #5058, #5063)

Cumulative Changes Since 7.1.2

This view combines the delta above with the customer-facing changes introduced in preview1. Changes already shipped in 7.1.1 or 7.1.2, including the user-agent configured-compatibility bits, are not presented again as new in 8.0, even though preview1's branch-cut baseline included them.

Added

  • SQL Server float16 vectors, SqlVector<Half> (net10.0 only), and per-connection Vector Type Support / SqlConnectionStringBuilder.VectorTypeSupport negotiation. The default is V2: modern .NET returns native float16 vectors rather than JSON strings. Use v1 for the previous float16 string contract or off for all-vector text results. .NET Framework can read float16 as text or widened SqlVector<float> values. Column-schema VectorBaseType and VectorDimensions identify negotiated native metadata. Parameters and bulk copy support native base-type conversion; vector TVPs are not added. Float16 requires server support and PREVIEW_FEATURES while in preview. (#4501)
  • Opt-in pooled transaction-isolation reset through Switch.Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.EnableTransactionIsolationLevelReset (default false). SqlClient-tracked isolation changes can reset to READ COMMITTED before reuse without an active enlistment/delegated root. Raw T-SQL changes alone are not tracked; known Synapse dedicated endpoints are excluded. Necessary resets add a round trip. (#96, #4330)
  • TimeOnly writes for bulk-copy DataRow/DataTable inputs and variant parameters. (net10.0 only; #4604)
  • Authentication EventSource diagnostics under keyword AuthenticationTrace (0x2000); use 0x2002 to include ordinary tracing. PII logging remains disabled for extension-owned requests. Correlation is best effort, and application-owned token callbacks are not covered. Treat captures as sensitive. See the Azure and Internal.Logging notes. (#1846, #4872)

Changed

  • Breaking runtime change: the modern implementation now requires .NET 10; .NET Framework 4.6.2 remains supported. netstandard2.0 reference/unsupported-platform assets do not restore runtime support for .NET 8 or .NET 9. (#4779)
  • Breaking networking defaults: omitted MultiSubnetFailover defaults to true for eligible TCP connections; TNIR defaults to false on .NET Framework. Explicit values take precedence. Native SNI remote-host connections may use TCP without Named Pipes fallback. Use an explicit protocol/keyword or the documented compatibility switches when the previous behavior is needed. See networking migration guidance. (#4927)
  • Breaking dependency change: Azure Attestation (Attestation Protocol=AAS) requires an explicit matching-version Azure extension; otherwise enclave setup fails. Credential types now come from Azure.Core but retain their Azure.Identity namespace. Remove older direct Azure.Identity references or upgrade to 1.21.0+; Azure.Identity.Broker needs 1.6.0+. (#4790, #4749)
  • Reference APIs match implementation accessibility/sealing, remove the nonexistent SqlBatchCommand.CanCreateParameter setter (net462 only), and restore the obsolete SqlParameterCollection.Add(string, object) overload and TriggerAction (net462 only). SqlParameterCollection.RemoveAt(int) now throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException for invalid indexes; character SqlMetaData construction in invariant mode requires an explicit LCID (net10.0 only). Update affected compile-time assumptions and exception handling. (#4832, #4890, #4874, #4457)
  • Managed driver assemblies now reside in lib/net462 and lib/net10.0, not duplicated RID-specific managed directories. Consumer builds warn with SQLCLIENT001 for mismatched family package versions; native SNI and independently versioned Server are excluded. (#4673, #4815)
  • Windows pool identity includes the Windows logon session, separating network-only impersonation sessions with identical local SIDs. Distinct sessions can create more pools. (Windows only; #4814)
  • Authentication registration and SqlAuthenticationInitializer move to Abstractions with forwarding for compatibility. Public configuration handlers and a net10.0 trim/AOT-analyzed asset support direct registration. Configured providers precede application registrations and Azure defaults; failed explicit configuration is not silently replaced by defaults. For explicit trimmed/Native AOT registration, disable both EnableAppConfig and EnableAzureExtensionDiscovery at publish time, and register the required providers. Runtime switch changes alone do not remove reflection. Enabled reflective paths require retained contracts and report warnings; this is not full-driver Native AOT support. The driver's retry/switch-override configuration remains separately gated on modern .NET. (#4816, #4860, #4821, #4697)
  • Source-generated vector/attestation JSON and targeted diagnostics, schema, discovery, and interop annotations reduce trimming/AOT warnings without claiming complete AOT support. (net10.0 only) (#4683, #4801, #4684, #4688, #4703)
  • Reduced Always Encrypted key-handling allocations/cache contention and converted async bulk-copy setup to native async/await. Key-store decryption remains serialized, and the per-row asynchronous bulk-copy loop is unchanged. (#4256, #4687)
  • Added reconnection database-context diagnostics. Reader documentation clarifies complete result consumption for trailing errors/InfoMessage; preparation and batch documentation clarify existing restrictions. These diagnostics/docs do not change effective async defaults, reconnection, or reader cleanup semantics. (#4130, #4723, #4729, #4726, #4878)

Fixed

  • Managed-SNI parallel TCP attempts tolerate one immediate address failure while another address succeeds, disposing unused sockets. (net10.0, managed SNI only) (#4929)
  • XML fragments beginning with text use UTF-16LE for streaming; bulk copy preserves money/smallmoney identity in sql_variant values. (#4757, #4727)
  • Configurable retry does not execute outside a transaction aborted by the original error. Non-default isolation levels are reasserted when pooled sessions reattach to the same ambient transaction. Pool pruning preserves in-flight acquisition/creation/replenishment and transaction-affine reuse, and reclaimed-connection soft counters remain accurate. (#4728, #4335, #4755, #4754, #4725)
  • Retry providers resolve in SqlClient's current AssemblyLoadContext; collectible contexts using managed SNI can unload. Native-SNI unloadability is not promised. (net10.0 only) (#4588)
  • Formatter-based SqlException serialization retains Errors and derived error properties, addressing .NET Framework remoting. Formatter serialization is obsolete on modern .NET; this is not guidance to deserialize untrusted data. (#1940, #4622)

Removed

  • Breaking compatibility change: SQL Server 2005 connectivity and Type System Version=SQL Server 2005 are removed, including legacy date/time and large-UDT projections. Remove that setting and consume current SQL Server type representations. (#4881)

Contributors

We thank the following public contributors for their contributions across the preview and this delta:

  • alaricd
  • charlesroddie
  • edwardneal
  • MaceWindu
  • RoccoPanunzio
  • sharpjs
  • shreyarao4
  • tomasfil
  • virzak

Target Platform Support

  • .NET Framework 4.6.2+ on Windows.
  • .NET 10.0+ on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
  • netstandard2.0 assets are for reference/unsupported-platform scenarios only.

Dependencies

Direct dependency minimums are shown below. Family and native SNI dependency ranges are [8.0.0, 9.0.0).

The table uses the official pipeline's default of not building Microsoft.SqlServer.Server, which selects SqlServerPublishedVersion=1.0.0 and dependency range [1.0.0, 2.0.0). Building Server instead selects its independent 1.1.0-preview1 version with a build suffix. No separate Server release is included in this milestone.
